### 1.1-1.3 Problem Analysis

The issue describes that the **verbose option** in hashin no longer makes sense because of a fundamental change in how package metadata is retrieved. 

**Technical Details:**
- Commit `66aa748a6d80e436283f26526b5af2b3b9a0d62f` switched from old PyPI API to pypi.org API
- Previously: Had to download each release file URL and run `pip` to get checksums
- Now: Digests (md5, sha256) are directly available in JSON at `.releases[<desired version>][N].digests.sha256`
- Example endpoint: `https://pypi.org/pypi/psycopg2/json`

**Problem Statement:** 
The verbose output still shows processing steps for individual URLs that are no longer needed since digests are obtained directly from the JSON payload.

### 1.4 Steps to Reproduce
1. Run hashin with verbose flag (`-v` or `--verbose`)
2. Observe verbose output showing URL processing steps
3. These URL processing steps are no longer necessary with the new API

### 1.5 Best Practices
- Understand current verbose output behavior
- Identify where URL processing logic exists in code
- Modify verbose output to reflect actual simplified process
- Maintain backward compatibility for verbose flag functionality

   186	Running tests with test coverage
   187	================================
   188	
   189	To run the tests with test coverage, with ``pytest`` run something like
   190	this::
   191	
   192	    $ pip install pytest-cover
   193	    $ pytest --cov hashin --cov-report html tests
   194	    $ open htmlcov/index.html
   195	
   196	
   197	Debugging
   198	=========
   199	
   200	To avoid having to install ``hashin`` just to test it or debug a feature
   201	you can simply just run it like this::
   202	
   203	    touch /tmp/whatever.txt
   204	    python hashin.py --verbose Django /tmp/whatever.txt
   205

   207	History
   208	=======
   209	
   210	This program is a "fork" of https://pypi.python.org/pypi/peepin
   211	``peepin`` was a companion to the program ``peep``
   212	https://pypi.python.org/pypi/peep/ but the functionality of ``peep``
   213	has been put directly into ``pip`` as of version 8.
   214	
   215	Future
   216	======
   217	
   218	If this script proves itself to work and be useful, I hope we can
   219	put it directly into ``pip``.
